theNeverTrueCase._: ⭐⭐ THE ANSWER WORTH THE ADD. A condition that has NEVER been true returns `na` on every bar — not 0 (which would read as 'it just happened') and not a large sentinel (which would read as a real distance). ⛔ 0 is the dangerous one: a screen written as `barssince(cond) < 5` would fire on EVERY bar for a condition that never occurred.

theOrdinaryCase._: 0 ON THE BAR THE CONDITION IS TRUE, counting up from there. No `na` anywhere once the condition has fired at least once.

_theVaryControl._: ⭐ A rare condition's counter must actually MOVE, or the raw channel above could be reading a constant and nobody would know. It ranges 5..19 across the window and rises by 1 per bar at the tail (17, 18, 19 on the last three), which is a counter doing its job.
